author: Associated Press
description:
Garcés Pérez, who was shot in his car by agents, is accused of striking officer with side mirror while trying to drive away

Federal prosecutors on Tuesday announced an assault charge against a Venezuelan delivery driver who was shot in his car by a federal immigration agent in Texas, accusing the man of striking an officer with his side mirror while trying to drive away.

Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was charged with one count of assaulting, resisting and impeding a federal officer, according to a criminal complaint. Garcés Pérez, whose attorney has said still has a bullet lodged in his back from the 20 September shooting, made an initial court appearance in an Austin federal court on Tuesday, according to the US attorney’s office in the western district of Texas.

Continue reading...
title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE agent in Texas charged with assaulting an officer

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Early works are beginning on the second stage of the long-awaited train line to Melbourne Airport – a 7.6km stretch of the train line from Albion, in Sunshine West, to Keilor East, where a new station will be built.

Anthony Albanese will be in Melbourne today with Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, to announce that site investigations, procurement and development work will begin in the coming weeks.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: Home Affairs orders ‘rapid’ stocktake of government cyber-systems after OpenAI hack

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
More than 100 people have said they were injured by the ride in California, which reaches up to 76mph

Six Flags has permanently shut down its embattled X2 rollercoaster in Valencia, California, the company announced on Tuesday, as a groundswell of past riders have come forward with allegations of serious injuries.

X2, a Magic Mountain park favorite, which reaches up to 76mph (about 122km/h) and has seats that can rotate 360 degrees, had been closed since mid-July.

Continue reading...
title: Six Flags permanently shuts down X2 rollercoaster after claims of brain injuries

author: Abené Clayton and agencies
description:
Douglas Carter, 71, who has spent more than four decades on death row, was released on bail until new trial begins

A Utah man who has spent more than four decades on death row was released from jail after newly analyzed DNA evidence showed that he was not connected to a 1985 homicide.

Douglas Stewart Carter, now 71, walked out of the Utah county jail late on Monday night after a judge ordered his release on bail. He will have to wear a GPS monitoring device until a new trial begins.

Continue reading...
title: Utah death-row prisoner released after new DNA analysis of 1985 killing

author: Cecilia Nowell
description:
‘Yellow 2120’ has been driven out of other Altadena neighborhood crawlspaces but he just keeps coming back

He’s back: the 550lb bear made famous after he took up residence under an Altadena home in November 2025 is wandering the Los Angeles neighborhood again after he moved in and out of the crawlspace of another home.

“Yellow 2120”, as the black bear has been tagged, was spotted in the crawlspace of a home on Minoru Drive on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Cute but unbearable’ freeloading bear discovered in another LA crawlspace

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Conservative majority temporarily lifts lower-court decision as liberal justices dissent from ruling

The Trump administration may deport immigrants to a “third country”, or a country other than their homeland, without providing them an opportunity to dispute due to humanitarian concerns, the supreme court said in a brief order on Tuesday.

The six-justice conservative majority of the high court temporarily lifted a lower court decision that determined immigrants being deported to a third country needed notice to argue they are at risk of persecution.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court allows Trump officials to resume deportations to third countries

author: Ariana Baio
description:
GOP senators lash out on Smith, who led criminal cases against Trump, with invective and inaccurate information

Former special counsel Jack Smith, who led two criminal cases against Donald Trump in 2023, faced attacks from Republicans in a wide-ranging hearing on Tuesday that included a basketball mix-up, a reference to the tooth fairy and accusations of perjury.

In the Senate judiciary committee hearing on Tuesday, the Republican senator Eric Schmitt, of Missouri, raised perjury allegations against Smith, seemingly over a mix-up about the Atlanta Hawks and University of Iowa Hawkeyes basketball teams.
title: ‘You make me want to throw up’: Republicans attack ex-special counsel Jack Smith at Senate hearing

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Over half of 260 workplace child fatalities between 2013 and 2023 lacked data on cause of death or the industry worked

Information is missing on over half of deaths at work of people under the age of 18 in the US because of significant gaps in child labor data, according to a government accountability office (GAO) report released on Tuesday.

The report found that between 2013 and 2023, an average of 24 children under the age of 18 died each year due to work-related incidents. Over half of the 260 child fatality cases did not contain detailed data on the cause of death or the industry the child worked in.

Continue reading...
title: Key data missing for half of US child labor deaths, official report finds

author: Associated Press
description:
Researchers say the IPO market was off to a solid start but tailed off in the third quarter

Smart ring maker Oura Inc says it is postponing a planned initial public offering due to market “uncertainty”.

In a Tuesday press release, Oura said it is delaying the stock market float “despite strong demand”.

Continue reading...
title: Smart ring maker Oura puts off initial public offering due to market ‘uncertainty’

author: Helena Horton and Vikram Dodd
description:
Head of counter-terrorism policing defends decision to bail five British men arrested in connection with incident

No explosive devices were found in three vans searched near RAF Fairford as part of a terrorism investigation but a quantity of petrol was recovered, police have said.

Five British nationals were arrested in the early hours of Sunday morning after a resident living near the Gloucestershire airbase reported suspicious activity involving three vans.

Continue reading...
title: No explosives found in three vans searched near RAF Fairford, say police

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
PM’s speech, written almost entirely alone, was full of radicalism but his biggest plans will have to wait until after the next election

  • Key takeaways from Andy Burnham’s conference speech

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Hope Again is the conference slogan. But what felt even more apt was Try Again.

Just forget about the last two years, after the party won a historic majority but where the mood never matched the achievement. Now, as conference delegates and MPs filed out of the hall after Andy
title: Burnham’s emotional solo act had Labour in raptures – but his promises will take time to come good

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Bank allows employees to delay being in workplace at least three days a week until 2027, if permission granted

Barclays has watered down its return-to-office plans after a major staff backlash, with the bank allowing some employees to wait until next year before having to be in at least three days a week.

The bank this summer announced the attendance requirement would come in for its 45,000 UK staff from 5 October, with more senior employees expected to come in for at least four days. That compares with current rules requiring staff to come in for two days.

Automatic exemptions of in-office attendance rules during school holidays and Christmas.

Capping in-office requirements at one day a week for any carers or people with disabilities.

Flexible start and finish times to allow for cheaper off-peak travel costs and to accommodate school
title: Barclays softens return-to-office plans for UK staff after backlash

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Pennsylvania has reported over 900 measles cases and four deaths as governor and health chief RFK Jr spar over data

A second measles death in the US has been announced on Tuesday by the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), as the country grapples with an outbreak affecting 47 states.

As of 24 September, a total of 3,659 measles cases have been confirmed by the CDC, with the two deaths having been confirmed on Tuesday. The confirmation did not specify in which states the deaths had occurred.

Continue reading...
title: CDC reports second measles death in US while excluding Pennsylvania deaths

author: Patrick Wintour
description:
Relations between the two countries soured in January when a UAE-backed force was defeated by Saudi Arabia in Yemen

Saudi Arabia is being urged to reconcile with the United Arab Emirates over Yemen as the price Riyadh must pay to form a military alliance capable of driving the Houthis back.

Relations between the UAE and Saudi Arabia in Yemen, where both had backed anti-Houthi forces, plummeted in January this year when a force with which it had been aligned – the separatist Southern Transitional Council (STC) – was attacked and defeated by Saudi Arabia in a move intended to squash its attempt to recreate a separate southern state. The UAE subsequently effectively quit Yemen.

Continue reading...
title: Saudi Arabia urged to reconcile with UAE to drive back Houthi separatists in Yemen

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Recreational jumpers used their training as paramedics to treat crash victims before ground crews arrived

A team of experienced skydivers recently dropped in to help at a plane crash they happened to witness in Wisconsin – and used their training as paramedics to treat a seriously injured victim before ground-based rescue crews arrived.

The single-engine plane carrying four people crashed in a cornfield near East Troy on Sunday, watched by the occupants of a Skydive Milwaukee aircraft who were preparing for an afternoon of recreational jumping.

Continue reading...
title: Team of skydivers drop in to help survivors of a plane crash in Wisconsin

author: Maya Yang
description:
Man, 57, was reportedly leaving A train at Utica Avenue station when stuck bag dragged him back and on to tracks

A man in Brooklyn, New York, died after his bag got caught between the doors of a subway train which then dragged him down.

On Monday, a man was leaving a Manhattan-bound A train at the Utica Avenue station in Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood when his shopping bag became caught between the subway’s doors.

Continue reading...
title: New York man killed after bag caught in subway train doors, police say

author: Reuters
description:
Clancy’s attorneys say a mistrial shouldn’t have been declared and a retrial would result in double jeopardy

Lindsay Clancy returned to court on Tuesday, as her lawyers sought to head off a retrial by having a judge find the Massachusetts woman not guilty of murder for the killing of her ⁠three young children in 2023.

Judge William ⁠Sullivan in Plymouth, Massachusetts, ​took up the issue after declaring a mistrial on 4 September, which occurred after a single juror prevented the 12-member jury from reaching a unanimous verdict on whether to convict Clancy or find her not guilty by reason ⁠of insanity.

Continue reading...
title: Lindsay Clancy returns to court after Massachusetts murder case mistrial

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Trans inmates sued the administration over the policy and, so far, two lower courts have blocked implementation

The Trump administration asked the US supreme court, on Monday, to allow it to deny gender-affirming care to transgender inmates in federal prisons, while litigation over the matter continues in lower courts.

In its latest emergency request to the high court, the solicitor general, D John Sauer, wrote that certain care, including sex-trait-modification surgeries, hormone therapy and social accommodations – such as undergarments, makeup, padding and wigs – “could no longer be justified as treatment for gender dysphoria”.
title: Trump admin asks supreme court to allow gender-affirming care denial to transgender prisoners

author: Steven Morris
description:
District judge orders record fine for region and says incidents of pollution cannot be tolerated

A water company has been ordered to pay a record fine of almost £8m for hundreds of sewage spills at popular bathing spots and sensitive habitats in Cornwall and Devon.

On one occasion, untreated sewage gushed through a harbour wall on a bank holiday weekend but South West Water (SWW) engineers took 10 hours to attend.

Continue reading...
title: South West Water fined £8m for hundreds of sewage spills in Cornwall and Devon

author: Kim Willsher in Paris
description:
More than 200 arrested while teachers join protest over class sizes, exhausting timetables and staff shortages

French teenagers blockading their schools in protest at class sizes, teacher shortages and long timetables have clashed with police, as politicians traded verbal blows over how to respond.

Demonstrations that began in Paris last week have escalated and spread across France, with the authorities reporting the arrest of 164 people on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: French students and police clash as school blockades turn violent

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
President of Marine Le Pen’s far-right party faces calls to resign over comments he allegedly wrote as a teenager

Jordan Bardella, the head of Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN), has claimed a “total war” is being waged against his party as he faces a political storm after the publication of antisemitic comments he allegedly wrote as a young party member.

Bardella, who is facing calls from political opponents to resign, said on Tuesday that the report by the investigative website Mediapart was false. To a standing ovation from his party’s lawmakers and senators at a meeting in parliament, he said the report was an attempt to damage his party as Le Pen tops the polls before th
title: National Rally’s Jordan Bardella rails at ‘war’ on party after antisemitism claims

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Mike Lee objected to the safeguard against the demolition of any presidential memorial Congress designates

  • US politics live – latest updates

A Republican senator has blocked a bipartisan bill that would have prevented Donald Trump from demolishing the Kennedy Center without the approval of Congress.

Mike Lee, of Utah, objected on Monday night when the Oregon Democrat Jeff Merkley asked the Senate to pass the Protecting Presidential Memorials Act by unanimous consent. The bill, co-written with the Alaska Republican Lisa Murkowski, would have banned the demolition of any presidential memorial designated by Congress, including the Lincoln and Jeffers
title: US senator blocks bill to ban Trump from demolishing Kennedy Center without Congress’s approval

author: Steven Morris
description:
Police and medics fear mother could be ‘extremely vulnerable’, after discovery in Bangor close to Menai strait on Sunday

Police are searching for the mother of a newborn baby whose body was found on a Welsh shoreline, fearing she may be ill or vulnerable.

A member of the public found the body of the child, whose age and sex have not been disclosed, close to the Menai strait in north Wales.

Continue reading...
title: Body of newborn baby found on Welsh shoreline, prompting search for mother

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Commonwealth tells high court its proposed laws to let users opt out of algorithms would ultimately have the same effect as the ban

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian government has conceded it implemented the “world-leading” under-16s social media ban before there was scientific consensus on the link between mental health harms and social media use, but argued the “credible risks” of issues such as addictive behaviours and anxiety justify the policy.

In its defence against a high court challenge of the ban, the government has also argued its proposed digital duty of ca
title: Australian government concedes no scientific consensus on social media harms for teenagers – but ‘credible risks’ justify ban

author: Josh Butler
description:
More than half of Australians want to see the country’s migrant intake lowered while One Nation’s primary vote climbs to 25%

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Coalition has failed to capitalise on growing criticism of Labor, with the opposition stuck at its lowest-ever primary vote in the Guardian Essential poll.

The poll also shows more than half of all Australians want immigration cut and have voiced support for hardline enforcement, such as forced deportation.

Continue reading...
title: Guardian Essential poll: Coalition’s primary vote sinks to lowest ever as majority support hardline immigration ideas

author: Penry Buckley
description:
You could be forgiven for thinking the inquiry has been a bit of a damp squib. But high-profile resignations are not the only measure of Icac’s success

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Many people watching the Independent Commission Against Corruption hearings in Sydney over the past two months have come to admire the forensic questioning of the counsel assisting the inquiry, Peggy Dwyer SC.

As she set out the complicated allegations in detail on the opening day in July, Dwyer emphasised the central role of electoral donations laws, observing: “Money in politics, as in other spheres of
title: Blackmail, ‘mafia boys’ and rants from a Beirut bedroom – after 10 weeks of theatre what might Icac deliver?

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
No excuses for next leader of party, Adam Bandt says, while Bob Brown warns they must also be able to take on Pauline Hanson and One Nation

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The former Greens leader Adam Bandt says the party’s new leadership team, which could be chosen as early as today, will face mounting pressure from grassroots members to block the Labor government from approving any new coal and gas projects “by whatever means”.

He told Guardian Australia there would be no excuses for the new leader, likely to be elected at a two-day retreat in Sydney which begins today, to allow the Albanese government to approve any new fossil fuel development.
title: Senior Greens figures say new leadership must stop Labor approving fossil fuel projects ‘by whatever means’

author: Helena Horton
description:
Private members’ club apologises after former employee exposes issue at its Shoreditch House venue

The Soho House private members’ club has launched an investigation after out-of-date food was mislabelled in one of its kitchens.

The club, which charges up to £4,500 a year for membership, has apologised after a former employee made a video on TikTok exposing the issue.

Continue reading...
title: Soho House launches investigation after out-of-date food mislabelled in kitchen

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Clarkson’s Farm star says broadcasters should make ‘bigger, fewer, better programmes’ in face of competition from streamers and digital platforms

Jeremy Clarkson has called on British broadcasters to merge into a single “Britflix” platform to survive, as he warned that senior producers were continuing to “drain away” from the cash-strapped TV industry.

The former Top Gear presenter said that having just finished filming the sixth season of his Amazon Prime show Clarkson’s Farm, there were now many members of the crew wondering where they would find their next job.

Continue reading...
title: British broadcasters should merge into single platform to survive, says Jeremy Clarkson

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Health secretary calls for medical and lifestyle details to be sent to doctors and AI to address ‘chronic disease epidemic’

Robert F Kennedy Jr laid out an expansive vision for collecting, sharing and analyzing US health information at a Maha event hosted by a close ally and outspoken anti-vaccine activist.

Medical and lifestyle data, from doctor’s visits to exercise, should be connected and shared with the government and independent researchers, where it can be searched by AI – including potential links between vaccines and health outcomes including autism and mortality, suggested Kennedy, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine skeptic.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr outlines expansive vision for collecting US health data at Maha event

author: Richard Luscombe and agencies
description:
Storm seems to have exposed segments of the Warren Sawyer, a wooden vessel that ran aground in 1884

The nor’easter storm that pummeled New England over the weekend looks to have exposed large segments of a 19th-century schooner shipwrecked in the so-called graveyard of the Atlantic.

The Warren Sawyer was sailing from New Orleans to Boston carrying cotton and scrap iron when the three-masted wooden vessel ran aground in Nantucket on 22 December 1884. Its captain and crew of seven were rescued and the ship began to break up after several weeks on the shoreline.

Continue reading...
title: Nor’easter unearths pieces of 19th-century shipwreck in Massachusetts

author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
description:
Decrees include extending ban on evictions of vulnerable people after 87-year-old was forced out of her home

Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government has approved a range of measures aimed at easing the country’s housing crisis, including extending a ban on evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, after a public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old disabled woman from her Madrid apartment last week.

Two decrees have been approved by cabinet but will need to be approved in Congress, where the coalition lacks a majority. The government has requested a special parliamentary session on Friday in the hope of getting the decrees passed as soon as possible.

Continue reading...
title: Spanish government approves measures to ease housing crisis after outcry over eviction

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Agent calls death of Haskins, who played the school principal in three programs, ‘a tragic loss’

The US actor Dennis Haskins – most known for co-starring in the popular Saved by the Bell television series franchise – has died, his agent confirmed on Tuesday. He was 75.

Alluding to Haskins’ Saved by the Bell character, the fictional high school principal Mr Richard Belding, agent Jay Schachter said in a statement: “It’s a tragic loss. Everyone loved Mr Belding, and those of us who got to know Dennis loved him even more.

Continue reading...
title: Dennis Haskins, US actor who played Mr Belding in Saved by the Bell, dies aged 75

author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Rome, From Mount Aventine will also visit Hong Kong and New York before it is expected to sell for record price

A JMW Turner painting of Rome that has been described as his “great love letter” to the city and has fleetingly returned there after almost 200 years is expected to set a new record when it goes up for sale in December.

One of the few works by Turner that remains in private ownership, Rome, From Mount Aventine will be on display at Palazzo Rondinini in central Rome from Tuesday to Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: JMW Turner’s ‘great love letter’ to Rome makes brief return to city before UK auction

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Average five-year fixed mortgage interest rate has hit 5.94%, its highest since October 2023, says Moneyfacts

  • Business live – latest updates

Demand for UK mortgages slumped to a 32-month low in August as buyers were deterred by rising costs linked to the war in Iran.

Just 54,918 mortgages for new home purchases were approved in August, the Bank of England reported on Tuesday, the lowest monthly total since December 2023.

Continue reading...
title: UK mortgage demand drops to 32-month low as Iran war drives up borrowing costs

author: Associated Press
description:
Local sheriff’s department announces new development related to disappearance of TV host’s mother in Arizona

Authorities are looking into the possibility of a new ransom note related to the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, nearly eight months after she went missing from her Arizona home, the Pima county sheriff’s department said.

The sheriff’s department and the FBI Guthrie taskforce were recently made aware of the possible ransom note as well as social media comments related to it, the statement from the sheriff’s department said on Monday. Investigators are working to determine its credibility.

Continue reading...
title: Officials investigate possible new ransom note in Nancy Guthrie case

author: Associated Press
description:
Four sailors injured during unexplained ‘mishap’ onboard USS Dwight D Eisenhower aircraft carrier

Two US navy aviators ejected as they were landing their plane on the USS Dwight D Eisenhower aircraft carrier off the coast of Virginia on Monday, and four sailors onboard the vessel were injured in what naval officials characterized as a “mishap”.

The two aviators, assigned to Carrier Air Wing 3, successfully ejected as “a mishap occurred during aircraft recovery operations” and were rescued by search and rescue personnel, the navy said in a short statement.

Continue reading...
title: Two US navy aviators eject while landing on carrier off Virginia

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Beauty specialist will open branded areas in 100 Marks & Spencer stores and will sell its products on chain’s website

Marks & Spencer is has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract younger shoppers.

The French retailer is set to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year.

Continue reading...
title: M&S links up with Sephora to lure younger shoppers

author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
description:
Ministers from Viktor Orbán’s former far-right government arrested after MPs vote to lift their immunity

Two ministers in Viktor Orbán’s former far-right government suspected separately of misusing millions of euros of public funds and taking millions more in bribes have been detained, hours after Hungarian MPs voted to lift their immunity.

Prosecutors said on Tuesday that Balázs Hankó, Orbán’s culture minister and still an MP in the former prime minister’s nationalist Fidesz party, was ​taken into custody late on Monday. Hankó is suspected of misappropriation of funds. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Continue reading...
title: Two former Hungarian ministers detained over suspected bribery and misuse of public funds

author: Associated Press
description:
• College sports have been upended by athlete payments

  • Critics say legislation does not go far enough

The Senate passed a sweeping bipartisan bill on Monday that would regulate college sports, an attempt to end “chaos” in an industry that has been upended by skyrocketing athlete payments and near-unrestricted transfers between schools.

The overwhelming 77-22 vote to pass the Protect College Sports Act is the strongest effort yet by Congress to set national regulations governing payments to college athletes for their name, image and likeness and how often they can transfer. It would give the NCAA new authority over those rules and limited antitrust protections to enforce them.

Continue reading...<
title: Senate passes bipartisan Protect College Sports Act amid ‘chaos’ in industry

author: Martin Belam
description:
Anthropic’s prospectus makes chilling claim as new revelations emerge about Muse and Astra models. Plus the silent movie rediscovered in the strangest of places

Good morning. Anthropic is telling investors that advanced AI could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, according to reports, as it prepares for a potential $2tn flotation. The warning inside the startup’s IPO prospectus, which has yet to be made public, was reported by Reuters and the Financial Times. The company has previously called for a slowdown in the breakneck development of AI technology.

What has Meta’s Muse AI done? When the consumer tech reviewer Matt Robb listed a keyboard on Facebook Marketplace, Muse accepted a lowball offer without permission, promised a buyer he was waiting inside and
title: Anthropic warns of AI ‘existential risk’ as concerns emerge over Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s model | First Thing

author: Adeshola Ore Community affairs reporter
description:
Independent MP Allegra Spender says the comments reinforce the need for stronger protection against hate speech

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s peak body for imams says it is “deeply concerned” about reports a Melbourne-based Islamic preacher called for followers to “take up arms against his enemies” and not take “Jews and the Christians for friends”.

The Australian National Imams’ Council (ANIC) released a statement on Tuesday after Nine newspapers revealed the preacher who goes by the name Abu Ahmad made the comments during a sermon in July.

Continue reading...
title: Imams’ council condemns Melbourne Islamic preacher’s call to ‘take up arms’ against enemies

author: Nathan Sanders and Bruce Schneier
description:
Though politicians are quiet about how they use AI, the book Rewiring Democracy examines how AI is starting to influence American politics

New campaign finance disclosure data shines a light on which US political campaigns are using AI tools and how much they are spending on them.

Candidates’, parties’, and committees’ spending reveals that AI is fast becoming an essential tool of politics. The candidates themselves are quiet about how they are using the technology in their own campaigns. It’s a sensitive issue that we have been tracking closely since we started writing our book, Rewiring Democracy, which examined how AI is beginning to influence politics. A September 2025
title: New campaign disclosures reveal how much American political campaigns spend on AI tools

author: Phoebe Davis and Daniel Boffey
description:
Freedom of information request finds six-month trial cost £320,000, used almost 100 police hours and led to just one – incorrect – alert

A six-month trial of live facial recognition (LFR) technology in London’s railway stations that cost more than £320,000 and almost 100 hours of police officers’ time ended in one false match against a watchlist of suspects and no arrests.

More than half a million faces were scanned between February and July this year in some of the capital’s busiest transport hubs during the British Transport Police (BTP) trial of the surveillance technology, which aimed to help catch offenders and people breaching court orders.

Continue reading...
title: Trial of live facial recognition in London stations ends with a false positive and no arrests

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Green energy entrepreneur plans rescue package for the group behind the Camden New Journal, Islington Tribune and Westminster Extra

The green energy entrepreneur and Labour donor Dale Vince is planning to launch a London-wide news operation, as part of a “rescue” of one of the capital’s most highly regarded local newspapers.

Vince, who has vowed to take on what he sees as rightwing bias in the UK media, said he would invest “whatever it takes” to support the loss-making group behind the Camden New Journal (CNJ), Islington Tribune and Westminster Extra.

Continue reading...
title: Dale Vince plans London-wide news operation to take on ‘rightwing bias’ in the media

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
Transport for NSW, bus operator and Rail, Tram and Bus union investigate after incident on Monday evening

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Investigations are under way after a teenage girl fell from a moving double-decker bus on to a busy road in Sydney’s northern beaches.

Emergency services were called to Manly Road at Seaforth on Monday evening after the teenager fell from the B-Line bus near the Spit Bridge.

Continue reading...
title: Sydney teen taken to hospital after falling from moving bus on northern beaches

author: Patrick Commins
description:
The Reserve Bank appears ready to push harder against inflation but it comes with a greater risk for the economy

The fight against inflation has entered a new, more dangerous phase.

For years, the Reserve Bank has been attempting, as gently as possible, to steer inflation back to its 2.5% target while trying to retain as many of the post-pandemic job gains as possible.

Continue reading...
title: Danger zone: why war in the Middle East has landed the RBA’s inflation fight in tricky territory

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Patrol dog’s handler resigned after it emerged Bart had died of heatstroke due to severe dehydration in nearly 101F heat

The recent death of a Tennessee sheriff’s office dog after being left in an outdoor kennel without water for a day and a half in excessive heat has prompted the animal’s handler to resign amid administrative and criminal investigations, according to authorities.

Bart had been a patrol dog specializing in suspect apprehension, tracking, searches and drug detection before his handler found him dead inside his outdoor kennel on 19 September, Julian Wiser, the Madison county sheriff, said in a social media video announcement.

Continue reading...
title: Death of Tenessee sheriff’s office canine leads to criminal investigation

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Lucy Powell’s comments come after US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, also expressed concerns and says foreign actor was ‘clearly’ behind plot

  • Rubio says foreign actor was ‘clearly’ behind suspected RAF Fairford plot

Iran has previously said it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target. But Iran’s embassy in London yesterday strongly rejected any speculation linking the country to the arrests of the five suspects near RAF Fairford.

The Guardian’s defence and security editor, Dan Sabbagh, has looked i
title: RAF Fairford: Labour’s deputy leader says ‘I trust our police’ after Trump questions decision to bail suspects – latest updates

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
PM to tell Labour conference he is prepared to make difficult arguments and have ‘honest conversation’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham will signal he is prepared to look at scrapping the pensions triple lock to fund a national care service, telling the Labour conference he will be willing to make difficult arguments to tackle the UK’s intractable issues such as social care.

Government sources have suggested the prime minister will signal his willingness to review the policy but stop short of a pledge to scrap it altogether. The Unite general secretary, Sharon Graham, said the move would be “electoral suicide”, with an end to th
title: Burnham to signal willingness to look at scrapping pension triple lock to fund social care

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
The 84-year-old underwent surgery after a collision with two teenagers on an electric ‘fat bike’ in the Illawarra

Former ABC broadcaster Margaret Throsby is recovering in hospital after she was struck by an electric “fat bike” while walking on a shared path in the Illawarra, south of Sydney last week.

Her daughter, musician and author Holly Throsby, said the 84-year-old required surgery after a high impact collision with two teenagers on a fat bike left her with an injured hip, thumb and head.

Continue reading...
title: Former ABC broadcaster Margaret Throsby recovering in hospital after being hit by ebike

author: Helena Horton
description:
Four-hour production featuring star-studded cast will be performed at London County Hall

A play based on the trial of the men who drugged and raped Gisèle Pelicot will come to London for one night only this November – and promises to feature a star-studded cast.

The four-hour production of The Pelicot Trial: Tribute to Gisèle Pelicot has been performed around the world, including in New York City and Avignon, the city in France where the trial took place. This autumn, it is coming to London County Hall, the home of Agatha Christie’s Witness for the Prosecution.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Jaw-dropping’ play based on Pelicot rape trial comes to London for one night

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
NHS trusts also report disruption to supplies last winter of co-codamol and blood pressure medication ramipril

Hospitals are being hit by shortages of key drugs used to provide pain relief, prevent blood clots and tackle high blood pressure.

Dozens of NHS trusts in England have encountered scarcities of aspirin, the painkiller co-codamol – a combination of paracetamol and codeine – and ramipril, a blood pressure tablet.

Continue reading...
title: Hospitals in England hit by shortages of common drugs such as paracetamol

description:
In today’s newsletter: New details suggest there is a counter-narrative to how events unfolded at the airbase used by the US

Good morning. Vehicles suspected of carrying explosives zipping across Britain, entirely unbeknownst to authorities, is a disconcerting prospect.

Initially, it seemed precisely this had occurred in Gloucestershire early on Sunday. A major attack on RAF Fairford appeared to have been scuppered by “pure luck”, a local farmer said, after she noticed suspicious vans and masked men on an otherwise deserted country lane. Had she not tipped off police, the vigilant villager believes the five men arrested on terror offences would not have been apprehended. That account prompted questions about whether police and security services had been caught off guard.

title: Tuesday briefing: Inside the suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford

But Andy Burnham’s colleagues are excited about the confident promise of new social care system that seven previous prime ministers have failed to deliver.
